headline: Red Sox look to rebound as the rivalry hits Yankee Stadium
morning_brew: Wednesday was a dead quiet day on the diamond for us, which gave the whole city a chance to actually breathe for once after the week we've been having. We are sitting at seventy-three wins as we turn the page toward the most critical stretch of the schedule. The boys have had a full day to reflect on the recent struggles and get their minds right, because there is no easing into this next phase with a trip to the Bronx staring us in the face.

My neighbor Rick has been pacing his driveway all morning, muttering about the strike zone and how the league office treats these Bronx matchups like a personal favor, but I told him to save the conspiracy theories for the postgame. We know what this rivalry means to every townie from here to the Cape, and I expect the intensity to be cranked up from the moment the first pitch leaves the hand tonight. It is about damn time we reminded those guys in pinstripes who actually owns the division.

I am looking for our hitters to come out swinging and put the pressure on their defense immediately. We have enough talent in that clubhouse to make a run at the top of the wild card standings, but it requires playing clean baseball in hostile territory. If we can grab the opener, the energy for the rest of the series is gonna be electric. Let's get back to playing our game and show them why we never count ourselves out until the final out is recorded.
